transcript:
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
- Live from NPR News, I'm Giles Snyder.
Justin Huang is returning to NVIDIA.
The chip makers board announced a decision
less than two weeks after Huang resigned,
amid an alleged Chinese spy scandal.
President Trump is taking credit for the move,
saying he was involved in brokering the deal.
NPR's Shannon Bond.
- Trump shrugged off questions about Huang's relationship
with this alleged spy,
and these broader national security questions
over whether China is illegally getting access
to NVIDIA's most advanced chips.
And look, these are the chips that are used to train
and run the most cutting AI models, cutting edge AI models.
And that is why this whole saga has blown up
into such a big scandal.
It really gets at the heart of the AI race
between the US and China.
- Following the announcement of Huang's return,
the Trump administration said it is blacklisting MegaSpeed,
the Singapore-based cloud company at the center
of the scandal also separately blacklisted
a Singapore subsidiary of Alibaba.
An Israeli medical charity says the expansion
of Israeli military checkpoints
and the occupied West Bank is risking lives.
NPR's Lauren Freya reports from Tel Aviv.
- Physicians for Human Rights Israel has published
interviews with 25 Palestinian paramedics,
including one who says Israeli soldiers prevented him
from reaching a wounded man nearby,
leaving him to bleed to death.
In a new report, the group cites a 350% spike
in such incidents, including violence directed
at medical workers themselves between 2022 and 2024.
Imran Anati, the report's author,
calls this collective punishment.
- By blocking an ambulance to evacuate a patient,
you're blocking the health care
to the whole Palestinian community.
- One Palestinian mayor says six of his residents
have died in ambulances delayed at checkpoints
over the past three years.
Asked about the report, the Israeli military told NPR
it works to facilitate safe passage of medical teams
subject to security assessment.
Lauren Freya, NPR News, Tel Aviv.
- The lawyer for the father and daughter pulled
from a crowded SeaTac airport jetway by ICE agents
over the weekend says they were in the country legally.
Kate Stone from member station KUOW reports.
- Now viral video shows agents wrestling Ricardo
Lourando Mendoza and Sofia Hernandez Meija to the floor
while they were trying to board
an Alaska Airlines flight on Saturday.
Homeland security says both overstayed visas
and Meija will face a felony charge
for allegedly throwing hot coffee.
But their attorney, Olia Katala,
says both hold valid work permits
and are allowed to live in the U.S.
while awaiting pending asylum and green card decisions.
- Congress created these legal pathways.
Sofia and her father were using them.
Washington Governor Bob Ferguson
says state officials are reviewing
whether agents violated a state law passed in March,
banning law enforcement officers from wearing masks.
For NPR News, I'm Kate Stone in Seattle.
- This is NPR.
The Democratic National Committee
says presidential hopefuls will be required
to denounce election spending by secret donors
to qualify for the party debates during the primary season.
The DNC oversees the party's primary process
as planning 12 debates.
Native ants play critical roles
in maintaining the fabric of many ecosystems,
but NPR's Ari Daniel reports that fabric
can unravel when invasive ants show up.
- Ecologist Defu Chen of the South China
Agricultural University and his colleagues
examined the long-term interactions
between native ant communities in Southeast China
and two nasty invasive species,
including the little fire ants.
When these ants were outnumbered, they played dead
and the other invasive species stopped assailing them.
But once there were four times as many,
they launched lethal attacks.
- Ultimately, one side will defeat the other.
- The little fire ants then turned to the native ants,
which they displaced or wiped out.
Chen says the results suggest it may be best
to counteract the invasive species early
before the native ants come under fire.
For NPR News, I'm Ari Daniel.
- China has unveiled the crew for its Shenzhou-24 spacecraft.
The China Man Space Agency announced a crew Tuesday,
saying a Pakistani astronaut will become
the first foreign astronaut to board China's space station.
The inclusion of Muhammad Sishan Ali
marks the first joint flight involving Chinese
and foreign astronauts in the history
of China's crewed space program.
Two Chinese astronauts will fly with him.
The spacecraft's scheduled to launch Wednesday morning.
This is NPR.

topics.text: Justin Huang returns to NVIDIA after resigning amid alleged Chinese spy scandal, Trump claims credit
Trump administration blacklists Singapore-based cloud company MegaSpeed and an Alibaba subsidiary
Physicians for Human Rights Israel reports Israeli checkpoints delaying Palestinian paramedics, risking lives in West Bank
Father and daughter pulled from SeaTac jetway by ICE agents say they were in the country legally
Washington Governor Bob Ferguson reviewing whether ICE agents violated state law banning law enforcement masks
DNC requires presidential hopefuls to denounce secret-donor election spending to qualify for debates
Invasive little fire ants overpower native ant communities in Southeast China, study finds
China names crew for Shenzhou-24, including first foreign astronaut, Pakistan's Muhammad Sishan Ali
